definitions.text: All money the campaign committee took in this cycle, from any source.
All money the campaign committee paid out this cycle.
What the committee had in the bank at the end of its latest report.
Individual contributions of $200 or less, which the FEC does not itemize by donor.
Money other political committees gave directly to the campaign. Different from outside spending, which never passes through the campaign.

Money a group spends on its own to support or oppose a candidate, without coordinating with any campaign. The FEC records which candidate each expenditure was about and whether it supported or opposed them.
Money moved in from a joint fundraising or earlier committee of the same candidate. It is counted in receipts but was not raised from donors this cycle.

items.text: Campaigns report to the FEC quarterly. The figures here run through 2026-06-30, the latest periodic report on file. The next report, the October Quarterly, is due 2026-10-15 and will cover through 2026-09-30.
items.title: The candidate totals are a snapshot, not live.

items.text: Outside groups report as they spend, so that table is usually fresher than the candidate totals. The two halves of this page are not as of the same date.
items.title: Outside spending is on a different clock.

items.text: The largest outside-spending committees were active in May 2026, before the Democratic primary on 2026-05-19. Their spending is part of this race's record but was not aimed at the November contest.
items.title: Much of the outside money went to the primary.

items.text: A transfer from another authorized committee counts as receipts. The source-of-funds section shows it separately so it can be set aside when comparing what each campaign raised from donors.
items.title: One line inside the receipts is not new donor money.

items.text: Candidates who have never filed a periodic report show blank fields. The FEC reports nothing for them, which is not the same as a confirmed $0.
items.title: Blank is not zero.

items.text: They come from the FEC's own deduplicated aggregate, which can take several weeks to absorb a 24-hour notice. Spending reported by notice in the last month may not appear yet.
items.title: The outside-spending totals can lag recent filings.
